## Install

The following packages must be installed

* readr
* ggplot2

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)

```

## Data Gathering

Some notes on how data was gathered from the source system (Meter Data Management). 

* only EV accounts with a full year of usage used (connect date prior to Oct 1 2025)
* full year worth of usage data
* standalone homes (no apts)

## Initial Load

Load the sample meters (primary and EV) and take a look at the usage curves. Datasets will store a full year of values so get a single month to make viewing easier. 

```{r load}

primaryMeter = read_csv("raw_data/ev/12479002_readings_10012025-10012026.primary.csv")
evMeter = read_csv("raw_data/ev/12479002_readings_10012025-10012026.ev.csv")

# treat as date - thanks Claude
primaryMeter$start_full = as.POSIXct(primaryMeter$start_full, format = "%m-%d-%Y %H:%M")
evMeter$start_full = as.POSIXct(evMeter$start_full, format = "%m-%d-%Y %H:%M")

primaryMeter[is.na(primaryMeter$value), ]
evMeter[is.na(evMeter$value), ]
```

```{r}

# view month of Sept 2026 - notice peaks
ggplot(data = primaryMeter[primaryMeter$start_full >= as.POSIXct("2026-09-01 00:00:00", tz = "America/Chicago"), ], aes(x = start_full, y = value)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1)

```
```{r}

ggplot(data = evMeter[evMeter$start_full >= as.POSIXct("2026-09-01 00:00:00", tz = "America/Chicago"), ], aes(x = start_full, y = value)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1)

```

## One Day

Get a single day's usage to look at a smaller amount of time. Note how the EV meter is 0 most of the time but then shows usage corresponding with when the primary meter also has an uptick. 

### EV demand

```{r}

quarterHour = ((40*.8 * 240)/1000)/4
fiveMinute = quarterHour/3

```

The lowest amount of demand (kW) on a level 2 EV charger is 7.68 kW - that is a 40 amp charger. In a 15 minute interval the total kWh would be: `quarterHour`. Assuming the charger was not on for the whole 15 minutes a 5 minute increment would be: `fiveMinute`. Safe to assume any usage over 1kWh the EV charger is on, while less than that it's in "idle" state. Idle may use some small amount of power. 


```{r}

singlePrimary = primaryMeter[primaryMeter$start_date == '09-02-2026', ]
singleEV = evMeter[evMeter$start_date == '09-02-2026', ]

ggplot() + 
  geom_line(data = singlePrimary, aes(x = start_full, y = value, color = "Primary Meter"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = singleEV, aes(x = start_full, y = value, color = "EV Charging"), linewidth = 1) + 
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Value", title="Primary and EV Charging") + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Primary Meter" = "blue", "EV Charging" = "red"),
    name="Legend"
  ) 
```

## EV Data

Not a lot can be done until the EV and primary meter data is merged. Do this using the `Label Data.rmd` file and then load in one of the combined files that includes EV labeling. 

```{r}

labeled_data = read_csv("labeled_data/ev/12479002_readings_10012025-10012026.primary.csv")

# create date field
labeled_data$start_full = as.POSIXct(labeled_data$start_full, format = "%m-%d-%Y %H:%M")

```

```{r}
# count how many EV charging values compared to the total
total_charge_sessions = nrow(labeled_data[labeled_data$EV == TRUE, ])

# percent of charging vs normal usage
total_charge_sessions/nrow(labeled_data)
```
Note the small EV charging session missed in the data below compared to the true EV line above. Session was from 7-7:30am and only used .62 kWh total. Well under the label threshold. Not a true charging session, likely "pre-heating" the car. 

```{r}
singleLabel = labeled_data[labeled_data$start_date == '09-02-2026', ]

ggplot(singleLabel, aes(x = start_full, y = value, color = EV, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = "red", `FALSE` = "blue"),
    labels = c(`TRUE` = "Yes", `FALSE` = "No"),
    name = "Charging Indicated"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Value", title="Primary Meter w/ EV Charging Flagged")
```

## Full Dataset

```{r}

# read in all files as one data set
files <- list.files(path = "labeled_data/", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE, recursive=TRUE)

fullDF <- read_csv(files, id = "source_file")

# print # of unique meters, shoudl be 100
length(unique(fullDF$meter_num))

# num rows matches expected intervals for 100 meters
nrow(fullDF) == 100*((365*24*4)-3)

```

Check min/max and NA values

Notes:

* No values below 0 (good)
* start times between 00:00 and 23:45 (good)
* Max = 32, that is odd on a residential account

```{r}

summary(fullDF)


```
4 rather large values on the same meter. Further investigation shows these are estimated after a period of connectivity loss on this device. This is common to make intervals sum to the total of the start/end readings. Removing these outliers prior to model training is best. 

```{r}

# max demand on a 200 amp service 240 Volts * 200 amps / 1000 = 48 kW
cutOff = ((240*200)/1000) * .25

ggplot(fullDF, aes(x = value)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "kWh with Outliers", x = "kWh")

# find large values
largeValues = fullDF[fullDF$value >= cutOff, ]

# trim based on cutoff and re-plot
trimmedFullDF = fullDF[fullDF$value < cutOff, ]

ggplot(trimmedFullDF, aes(x = value)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "kWh without outliers", x = "kWh")

```

Class imbalance of EV=TRUE vs FALSE. EV charging makes up about 2.7% of the total data. XGBoost should be able to work with this as long as training/test/validation datasets keep the same ratio between them. 

```{r}
# count how many EV charging values compared to the total
total_charge_sessions = nrow(fullDF[fullDF$EV == TRUE, ])

# percent of charging vs normal usage
total_charge_sessions/nrow(fullDF)
```
